column2: The commands and feedback a harness gives the model, which are **part of the policy** because they change how well the same model does the task.
A third gate outcome, escalate, that is a **deny for effects** but is recorded as an escalation and counted apart, so a **human queue** can be built from the ledger.
A model that scores the next token given everything before it, so a reply's probability is the **product of its tokens' conditional probabilities**.
A property of inference kernels whose results **don't depend on the batch size**, removing one cause of nondeterminism at a **cost in throughput**.
The **calendar day in UTC**, [00:00, 24:00), over which G3 counts budgeted actions, named explicitly in config as `budget_day_tz`.
A tokenizer built by repeatedly merging the **most frequent adjacent pair** of symbols, whose **ordered merge list** is applied in order to encode new text.
The principle that **every access to every object** must be checked for authority; in tinyharness, no effect without an **allowing gates record** for that action earlier in the same run.
A contract term **no code reads** from the contract, which records the promise **without enforcing it**.
The gate rule that an action runs **only if every gate allows** it, while **every gate still runs** and records its verdict and reason.
A rule that **bans a capability**, such as reading a clock, rather than only requiring the same output for the same input.
Every tinyharness module that can change the world, record evidence, call out or grant authority, which the strategy and the gate table **must not import**.
The survey's **seven harness layers**: Execution environment, Tool interface, Context and memory, Lifecycle and orchestration, Observability, Verification and evaluation, Governance and security.
A mechanism that watches a system's execution step by step and **stops it before a step** that would violate the policy.
The principle that when the ledger (what the harness says it did) and the witness log and snapshots (what happened) disagree, **the witness wins**.
The gate table's form of fail-safe defaults: a gate that raises, or returns a malformed answer, **is a deny for that gate**, and the other gates still run.
Basing access decisions on **permission rather than exclusion**, so that a mistake or an unanticipated case results in **refusal, not in access**.
Safe actions a gate denies, over all safe actions; a gate carries information only if its **catch rate beats this rate**.
Reply positions where the next token has **probability 1**, encoded with **no draw**, as in the toy model everywhere but the verdict.
How much of each action a harness can **check on its own before it happens**, which shrinks as the model owns more of the control flow.
Temperature 0: always take the **most probable token**, breaking ties by the lower index.

Everything in an agent's loop **except the model's weights**: what the model is shown, which actions it may propose, which proposals may execute, what is recorded, and what happens when something fails.
A **per-layer report** of a harness, after the survey's reporting table, giving the configuration to reproduce or judge it and the **failure evidence** it keeps.
A policy that **relates several runs** rather than judging one execution, such as untrusted-data monotonicity's comparison of a clean run with an injected one.
A key carried by every delete that the provider remembers once applied, so the same key sent again returns **already_applied** instead of deleting twice.
An opened run with no closing record whose next record is a **recovered** that names it, the only open run the loop grammar accepts.
A property that **something good eventually happens**, which no finite prefix can violate, so **no execution monitor can enforce it**.
The score of one vocabulary token at the next position: the **dot product** of the hidden state with that token's row of the output matrix.
The **regular language** of legal runs: each run's records, read in order as event names, must form a word of it, which a **deterministic finite automaton** checks in one pass.
The fraction of **non-equivalent mutants**, small syntactic changes to a program, that a test suite kills.
A cut that keeps the **shortest prefix** of tokens, in decreasing probability, whose total probability is **at least `top_p**, and renormalizes.
A mutant that returns exactly what the original returns for every input, so only a test that **watches its effects** can kill it.
A comparison in which every arm sees **exactly the same inputs**, so the difference between arms is due to the arm alone.
The chance that **at least one of k** samples succeeds, the right measure when a person picks the best try.
The chance that **all k independent trials** of the same task succeed, estimated without bias from n trials with c successes as **C(c, k) / C(n, k)**.
The XACML role that evaluates a request against policy and **returns a decision**; in tinyharness, `gates.evaluate`.
The XACML role that intercepts the access, asks the PDP and **carries out its decision**; in tinyharness, `run_once`.
The XACML role that **supplies attribute values**; in tinyharness, the fresh provider read plus `Config` that build the facts dict.
The regular expression that cuts text into words, numbers, punctuation runs and whitespace, each with at most one leading space, before any merge, so **no token crosses a piece**.
StateFlow's term for carrying which step of a task a run is in through **explicit states and transitions**, so the code knows it rather than the model.
One mechanism that mediates every reference a subject makes to an object, and must be **always invoked, tamperproof, and small enough to be analyzed and tested**.
A re-run of the strategy and the model over recorded days of history, with what was regretted afterwards, under **several thresholds at once**.
Reproducing a run's model decisions by reading **recorded raw output** back through the same parser, **failing closed** with SKIP when a call doesn't match its recorded line.
The property that a strategy's value **depends only on the logged facts**, so re-running it in replay is evidence about what live did.
A frozen record of a run's goal, scope, limits, allowed models, stop terms, required evidence and escalation, fixed before the run and **hashed into `run_start**.
The invariant that every run's records **stay within the contract** hashed into its `run_start`: actions within the maximum, mode as declared, models within the allowed set.
A property whose every violation shows in some **finite prefix** that no continuation can repair: **nothing bad ever happens**.
A run that goes through every phase, gates included, with the live-mode gate **denying every action**, so nothing is deleted.
The divisor applied to logits before softmax: below 1 it sharpens the distribution, above 1 it flattens it, and it **never changes the order** of the tokens.
The design rule that every property a safe agent needs holds **because of the harness**, whatever the model proposes.
A byte string from a fixed vocabulary; its id is its index in that vocabulary, and the model **sees only ids**, never characters.
A cut that keeps the **k most probable tokens** and renormalizes.
The rule that a delete whose outcome is unknown **may have been applied**, so it is recorded as unknown and settled later by **reconcile** from the provider's truth.
The checker's record of every call the harness made to the provider, **written by the checker** rather than the harness.
A system that orchestrates models and tools through **predefined code paths**, as opposed to an agent, which lets the model direct its own process and tool use.
The database-logging rule, carried over to the ledger, that the record of a change must be in the log **before the change reaches the data**.
